candidates.attacker_control: A remote client controls the Dubbo frame header's lower five serialization bits and the entire body. No authentication or signature is required by the core Dubbo protocol; the optional TokenFilter only applies when a token is configured.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: CodecSupport does reject mismatched JDK/native-Java IDs 3, 4, and 7, so switching directly to Java serialization is not the issue here. The bundled SerialDetector blacklist does not cover Kryo/FST/fastjson and defaults to disabled with an empty list. If a deployment omits the alternative serializer extensions, getSerializationById returns null and the request is rejected. all/pom shows the standard shaded artifact includes fastjson, FST, Kryo, and JDK serialization modules. A suitable gadget chain is still required for RCE.
candidates.impact: Defeats the configured serialization setting as a security boundary and permits attacker-chosen deserialization paths. Depending on classpath gadgets and serializer behavior, this can lead to remote code execution, arbitrary class instantiation, or denial of service. No runtime exploitation was performed or confirmed.
candidates.prerequisites: A reachable Dubbo provider port using the default Dubbo codec; at least one non-JDK serializer extension on the provider classpath (the all-in-one artifact bundles fastjson, FST, Kryo, and JDK modules); and a classpath gadget for code execution. Initial decoding occurs before service-path routing, so a valid exported service name is not needed for the deserialization attempt itself.
candidates.root_cause: CodecSupport.getSerialization(URL, Byte) compares the network-supplied serialization ID with the provider URL's configured serialization only when the ID is 3, 7, or 4. The wire ID is taken from the Dubbo request header, so non-JDK IDs such as 6 (fastjson), 8 (Kryo), and 9 (FST) are accepted even when the provider configured hessian2 or another serializer. The selected object inputs then deserialize class/object data from the request body without an allowlist.
candidates.title: Attacker-controlled Dubbo serialization ID bypasses configured serializer validation
candidates.trace: DubboCodec.decodeBody extracts proto from the request header and, with decode.in.io defaulting to true, calls DecodeableRpcInvocation.decode. That calls CodecSupport.getSerialization(channel.getUrl(), proto). Because the mismatch check in CodecSupport is gated to IDs 3/7/4, an attacker can select ID 8, 9, or 6 and reach KryoObjectInput.readClassAndObject, FstObjectInput.readObject, or FastJsonObjectInput.JSON.parse on attacker-controlled bytes. Kryo registration is not required (registrationRequired defaults false), and the FST/fastjson readers also lack a class allowlist. This bypasses the configured-serialization boundary and causes untrusted object deserialization.
candidates.unverified: No build, test, or runtime execution was performed. Kryo, FST, and fastjson dependency internals are not present in the snapshot, so their exact class-resolution and gadget behavior is inferred from source call sites rather than inspected. Extension registration resources under META-INF/dubbo are not visible in the provided tree, so runtime activation of these serializer extensions is inferred from annotations and packaging. No concrete gadget or exploit was reproduced.
candidates.weakness_type: Deserialization of untrusted data (CWE-502); improper input validation (CWE-20)

coverage_summary: Reviewed the 876 model-visible repository files using source listing, text search, and bounded reads, with emphasis on Dubbo codecs, serialization modules, generic/HTTP/Telnet paths, QOS, registry, and configuration. get_source_scope reported no over-size, sensitive-name, or symlink exclusions. get_relation_scope reported 866 indexed files (10 missing), 744 Java files, no parse errors, and 14,442 unresolved calls; it provides syntactic navigation only, with no control-flow, data-flow, or semantic resolution. The review traced the default Dubbo request decode path through CodecSupport and the Kryo/FST/fastjson serializers, and checked the opt-in SerialDetector protections and alternative deserialization paths. No build, tests, scanners, or exploit payloads were run.
limitations: Static source review only; no runtime reachability or exploitability proof.
The relation index is partial and syntactic: 10 files are missing and 14,442 calls are unresolved; no data-flow or control-flow analysis was available.
Dependency sources for Kryo, FST, fastjson, Hessian-lite, Spring, and the servlet/Jetty stack are not in the snapshot, so their internal class filtering and gadget behavior are not verified.
SPI registration files under META-INF/dubbo are not visible in the source tree, so extension activation and packaged-runtime presence are inferred from annotations and pom packaging only.
Coverage was targeted rather than line-by-line for all 876 files; test and resource files are sparse and no runtime configuration was inspected.

rejected_leads.lead: GenericFilter.nativejava path reaches NativeJavaObjectInput.readObject with the SerialDetector blacklist disabled by default
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible separate deserialization path, but it depends on GenericFilter SPI registration and a reachable one-argument service method; not selected because the serializer-ID bypass does not require that filter or a target method.

rejected_leads.lead: HTTP protocol HttpInvokerServiceExporter uses an ObjectInputStream for request bodies
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible separate Java-deserialization issue, but requires the service to be exported over the non-default http protocol; it is a distinct root cause and was not selected.

rejected_leads.lead: Telnet InvokeTelnetHandler parses attacker JSON with fastjson before service lookup
rejected_leads.reason: The source shows JSON.parseArray on remote telnet input, but the fastjson module implementation and autoType behavior are not in the snapshot; no source-level confirmation of unsafe polymorphic deserialization.

rejected_leads.lead: QoS and Dubbo telnet management endpoints expose unauthenticated commands
rejected_leads.reason: QoS defaults to local-only and its visible commands are administrative; telnet invoke is an intended management surface. This is a deployment/authentication concern rather than the strongest concrete code defect.

rejected_leads.lead: ScriptRouter uses a ScriptEngine to evaluate routing rules
rejected_leads.reason: Execution requires control of registry/router configuration, which is a higher-privilege prerequisite than a direct network client; not selected.

summary: The strongest source-supported issue is an incomplete serialization-ID validation check in CodecSupport. The Dubbo wire header carries an attacker-chosen serialization ID, but getSerialization only verifies that ID against the provider's configured serialization for JDK IDs 3, 7, and 4. IDs for Kryo (8), FST (9), and fastjson (6) are accepted regardless of configuration, and their object readers have no class allowlist. This creates a remote deserialization boundary bypass in the default Dubbo protocol. No build, test, or runtime confirmation was performed.
